messages:
Maya Chen: Quick question — if a request arrives with both `Authorization: Bearer <token>` and `X-Api-Key: sk_...` (we're seeing some proxies pass both), which do we consider authoritative? Also what happens if `X-Project-Id` is missing but an org-scoped key is present?

Liam O'Connor: Short answer: we prefer Authorization bearer tokens for user-scoped auth, then X-Api-Key for service keys. If both present we validate Authorization first and only fall back to X-Api-Key if Authorization is absent/invalid.

Selena Park: To add: for org vs project scoping we currently do: 1) if X-Project-Id present, use it; 2) else if key is project-scoped, use key's project; 3) else if key is org-scoped, apply org fallback. So missing X-Project-Id + org-scoped key => valid but project inferred as null and permissions limited.

Gabe R.: Example headers we've seen from the proxy: ```
Authorization: Bearer eyJ...
X-Api-Key: sk_live_abc123
X-Forwarded-For: 10.0.0.1
``` In this case we authenticate with the bearer token and ignore the X-Api-Key for identity resolution.

Maya Chen: OK — follow-up: during key rotation we have an overlap period where both old and new keys are valid. Does the fallback logic treat stale/rotated keys differently? I.e., if Authorization fails and X-Api-Key is the old key within grace period, do we accept?

Liam O'Connor: Yes — we accept rotated keys within the configured grace window (default 5m). The flow: validate key against active set -> if not found, check pending/rotating keys -> if found and within grace window, accept but emit telemetry tag `auth:key:rotating`. After grace window they are rejected.

Selena Park: Note: when we accept a rotating key we also surface a warning header back to callers: `X-Auth-Warning: key-rotating` so clients can log and migrate. We should document that in the API contract.

Maya Chen: What about response codes: do we return 401 vs 403 for missing vs present-but-insufficient scope? Need exact wording for SDK docs.

Liam O'Connor: Policy: 401 if no valid credential was presented (including expired/unknown). 403 if credential is valid but lacks permission for resource/operation. Implementation nuance: if bearer token malformed -> 401; bearer valid but role missing -> 403. If proxy strips project header but key is org-scoped and lacks project permission -> 403.

Gabe R.: Small gotcha: some proxies rewrite Authorization and drop X-Api-Key. We should log header-stripping events with `infra-bot` so we can correlate. infra-bot: deploy-hook detected header-strip in ingress-nginx at 2026-03-05T15:12:02Z for host prod-app-1 :thumbsdown:

Maya Chen: Good call. Can infra add a trace/span label when header-strip happens? That will help debugging auth failures that look like 401s.

infra-bot: Noted. I'll add `ingress.header_strip=true` tag on the next rollout for nginx.

Selena Park: For the API contract docs: propose adding a table: precedence, behavior, example header sets, returned status codes and `X-Auth-Warning` semantics. Also include sample curl snippets for common cases.

Maya Chen: I'll draft the docs and a tiny compatibility test for the SDKs that asserts precedence (Authorization over X-Api-Key) and that rotating keys emit the telemetry flag.

Liam O'Connor: If you want a quick check, I'll wire up a small e2e in the auth-integration job and mark it as optional for the canary.

Maya Chen: Awesome — pinging @Liam in the PR when ready. Thanks! :pray:

Gabe R.: One more: should we normalize header names (X-Api-Key vs x-api-key) in ingress so middleware doesn't get confused? Might be worth a small middleware change to canonicalize.

Selena Park: Agreed — canonicalize to lower-case internally and strip leading/trailing whitespace. I'll add that to the PR.

Maya Chen: Thanks everyone. Action items: (1) Maya to draft docs + test, (2) Liam to add e2e check, (3) Selena to canonicalize header parsing, (4) infra-bot to add header-strip span tagging.

Liam O'Connor: I'll open a PR for the e2e with a test matrix tomorrow.

Maya Chen: Closing loop here — will drop link to PR once created.
